records.query: Need the specific antibiotic name, dose, and duration to confirm the temporal and causal link to the cholestatic injury pattern (elevated ALP, AST, INR). Also require eosinophil count and autoimmune hepatitis serologies (ANA, ASMA, anti-LKM) to distinguish drug hepatotoxicity from an autoimmune flare, since the polyclonal gammopathy without monoclonal component already reduces concern for myeloma progression.

Need the patient's liver function tests (ALT, AST, ALP, bilirubin), complete blood count with eosinophil count, and autoimmune/viral hepatitis serologies to differentiate hepatocellular from cholestatic injury and exclude alternative causes, as these are core for confirming antibiotic hepatotoxicity.

records.query: Need the patient's autoimmune hepatitis serologies (ANA, anti-SMA, anti-LKM1, IgG) and liver ultrasound to confirm hepatomegaly and exclude biliary obstruction, as these are core to differentiate antibiotic hepatotoxicity from autoimmune flare and structural causes.

bindings.label: 50-year-old female presented with abdominal pain, nausea, and progressive fatigue starting a few weeks before hospitalization
Symptoms began a few weeks before hospitalization, following treatment with oral antibiotics for a dental infection
Medical history included smoldering myeloma (diagnosed weeks before admission), autoimmune thyroiditis (since 2018), and Sjogren's syndrome (since 2020)
Physical examination showed normal vitals, enlarged liver, and bilateral leg edema
Laboratory tests show elevated ALP, AST, GGT, and INR with normal ALT and bilirubin (cholestatic pattern)
Viral hepatitis serology is negative and leukocytosis is present
Serum protein electrophoresis shows polyclonal gammopathy without a monoclonal component
Serum tryptase was elevated at 42 ng/mL and the bone marrow aspirate showed mast cell infiltration
